== Biography == 
Patterson was an only child who grew up in the [[Bayswater]] section of central London.<ref>Chapter 8; ''The Man Who Solved the Market'' by Gregory Zuckerman</ref> Patterson received his B.A. and Ph.D. in mathematics at [[Cambridge University]].<ref name = BI-homepage /> His doctoral advisor was [[John G. Thompson]].<ref>
{{Cite web
 | url = https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=26484
 | title = Nicholas Patterson - the Mathematics Genealogy Project
}}</ref> He initially worked for the British code-breaking agency [[GCHQ]] and the [[Institute for Defense Analyses|Center for Communications Research]] in Princeton.<ref>
{{Cite web
 | url = https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/news/radcliffe-magazine/man-who-breaks-codes
 | title = The Man Who Breaks Codes
 | website = Radcliffe Magazine
 | date = 2017-01-30
 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190701204253/https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/news/radcliffe-magazine/man-who-breaks-codes
 | archive-date = 2019-07-01
}}</ref>

Following this [[cryptology]] work, Patterson worked at the quantitative trading firm [[Renaissance Technologies]].<ref name="newyorker">
{{cite magazine
 | last1 = Mayer | first1 = Jane | date= 19 March 2017
 | url = http://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2017/03/27/the-reclusive-hedge-fund-tycoon-behind-the-trump-presidency
 | title = The Reclusive Hedge-Fund Tycoon Behind the Trump Presidency
 | magazine = The New Yorker
}}</ref>

In 2001, Patterson joined the Center for Genome Research at [[MIT]], the [[Whitehead Institute]]. He briefly worked on gene expression data applied to cancer before switching to the study of human genetics.<ref name = BI-homepage />

In 2012, Patterson developed [[ADMIXTOOLS]], a software package written in [[C (programming language)|C]] that is currently widely used by population geneticists.<ref name="Patterson 2012">{{cite journal |vauthors=Patterson N, Moorjani P, Luo Y, Mallick S, Rohland N, Zhan Y, Genschoreck T, Webster T, Reich D |title=Ancient admixture in human history |journal=Genetics |volume=192 |issue=3 |pages=1065–93 |date=November 2012 |pmid=22960212 |pmc=3522152 |doi=10.1534/genetics.112.145037 }}</ref>

=== Chess ===
Nick Patterson was a child [[chess prodigy]].<ref name = Chen-NYT /> He won the [[Irish Chess Championship]] in 1969. In a long game in the [[19th Chess Olympiad|Chess Olympiad of Siegen]] in 1970, where he played top board for Ireland, he met the Danish grandmaster [[Bent Larsen]], who was one of the top 10 players in the world at the time, and managed to make a draw as black after 93 moves.<ref name = chessgames-NJP />
